name: Four Verts Takeover vs Two-High
situation: 2nd & 8, +45, snapped at tempo against a two-high shell that hasn't settled its rotation

summary.motive: Attack a two-high shell's structural weakness — the open middle third — with four simultaneous verticals and sideline takes, letting the pre-snap MOFO read dictate a seam shot before the safeties can squeeze.
summary.whyItWorks: Sideline takes pin both quarters corners outside so no help can rotate in, and the mirrored seams force the middle-third safety to defend two routes with one pair of eyes; tempo removes the rotation adjustment entirely.
summary.failureMode: Cover 6 or a single-high rotation after motion that puts three deep defenders over four verticals, plus a pass rush that forces the QB off his MOFO read before the seam window opens.

beats.title: 1. The Pre-Snap MOFO Read
beats.text: Kelly's QB confirms both safeties are split before the snap — the middle of the field is mathematically open. Four verticals is the only call needed: the picture alone dictates where the ball will go.

beats.title: 2. Sideline Takes Pin the Quarters
beats.text: X and Z win their press releases and stack the corners up the sidelines. In true quarters both corners must carry their verticals, which means zero help can rotate toward the seams.

beats.title: 3. Attacking the Middle-Third Leverage
beats.text: The safety’s eyes bounce between two mirrored seams he can’t defend simultaneously. H stems to the inside shade — the one leverage a two-high shell structurally cannot give a single defender.

beats.title: 4. Takeover Complete
beats.text: The QB delivers off his hitch before the safeties can squeeze, and the catch lands in the MOFO void at 15+ yards. Tempo makes it worse: the next snap comes so fast the shell has no time to adjust its rotation rules.

relations.tell: All four receivers release vertically off the snap with sideline takes and zero intermediate cuts — the QB’s eyes lock on the MOFO window before anyone breaks.
